examples.question_text:
Calculate by partitioning:
(a) $969\div3$ into place-value parts
(b) $1836\div6$ into convenient multiples.

A student starts $4284\div7$ by splitting $4284$ into $4000+284$.
(a) Explain why this is unhelpful.
(b) Choose useful parts and calculate.
(c) Show a different useful partition giving the same answer.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $4000$ is not divisible by $7$, so this part is not easy to divide exactly.

(b) $4284=4200+84$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4284\div7\\&=(4200\div7)+(84\div7)\\&=600+12\\&=612\end{aligned}$

(c) $4284=3500+700+84$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4284\div7\\&=(3500\div7)+(700\div7)+(84\div7)\\&=500+100+12\\&=612\end{aligned}$

Both partitions total $4284$ and all their parts divide exactly by $7$.

examples.question_text:
Four identical event passes cost $3268$ points altogether.
(a) Find the cost of one pass by repeated halving.
(b) Check by partitioning.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Divide by $2$, then by $2$ again.
$\begin{aligned}3268\div2&=1634\\1634\div2&=817\end{aligned}$

One pass costs $817$ points.

(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3268\div4\\&=(3200\div4)+(68\div4)\\&=800+17\\&=817\end{aligned}$

One pass costs $817$ points, the same answer.

examples.question_text:
A learner writes $4936\div8=(4800\div8)+(136\div8)=600+16=616$.
Find the error and correct the working.
examples.solution_text:
The partition is useful, but $136\div8=17$, not $16$, because $8\times17=136$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}4936\div8\\&=(4800\div8)+(136\div8)\\&=600+17\\&=617\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: 969 = 900 + 60 + 9; dividing each part by 3 gives 300 + 20 + 3 = 323. 1836 = 1800 + 36; dividing by 6 gives 300 + 6 = 306. Both adapt the supplied syllabus partitioning method.

4000 = 7 × 571 + 3, so it does not divide exactly by 7. 4200 + 84 = 4284 and their quotients are 600 + 12 = 612. The alternative 3500 + 700 + 84 also totals 4284 and gives 500 + 100 + 12 = 612. This follows the supplied unsuitable-partition explanation and alternative-partition example.

Halving 3268 gives 1634; halving again gives 817. Independently, 3268 = 3200 + 68, and division by 4 gives 800 + 17 = 817. Four passes at 817 points total 3268 points. The identical-item context and repeated-halving method directly adapt the supplied laptop example.

4800 + 136 = 4936. 4800 ÷ 8 = 600 and 136 ÷ 8 = 17 because 8 × 17 = 136. Thus the erroneous part-quotient 16 must become 17, giving 617; 8 × 617 = 4936. The repair uses syllabus-supported partitioning and the multiplication–division connection.
